questions.question: Blue, blue-green and green together make which colour scheme?
questions.memo: Neighbouring colours on the wheel form an analogous scheme.

CA.G8.VAE.A2.title: Design principles
CA.G8.VAE.A2.description: Visual Arts (CAPS G8) — Art elements & design: Design principles.
CA.G8.VAE.A2.recovery_strategy: Design principles — balance, contrast, pattern, proportion, emphasis — guide how you arrange an artwork.

questions.question: Design principles are used to…
questions.memo: Principles organise the elements into an effective composition.

questions.question: 'Rhythm' as a design principle is created by…
options: repeating elements to lead the eye through the work
questions.expected: repeating elements to lead the eye through the work
questions.memo: Visual rhythm uses repetition to move the eye through an artwork.

questions.question: 'Movement' in design means…
options: the way the eye is guided around the artwork
questions.expected: the way the eye is guided around the artwork
questions.memo: Movement directs the viewer's eye on a path through the composition.

questions.question: 'Unity' (harmony) in design means…
options: all parts look like they belong together
questions.expected: all parts look like they belong together
questions.memo: Unity makes the parts feel like a coherent whole.

questions.question: Balance, contrast, pattern, proportion and emphasis are all design principles.
questions.memo: These are core design principles for arranging elements.

questions.question: Asymmetrical balance means…
options: the two sides differ but still feel balanced
questions.expected: the two sides differ but still feel balanced
questions.memo: Asymmetrical balance uses different elements that still feel evenly weighted.

questions.question: Repeating shapes to lead the eye creates visual ____.
questions.memo: Repetition creates visual rhythm.

questions.question: Emphasis creates a…
questions.memo: Emphasis makes a focal point that draws the eye.

questions.question: Good proportion keeps the sizes of parts looking believable.
questions.memo: Proportion balances the relative sizes of the parts.

questions.question: An artist repeats a triangle motif getting smaller across the page. This creates…
questions.memo: Repeating a changing motif creates rhythm and a sense of movement.

questions.question: Which principle stops one part overpowering everything else unfairly?
questions.memo: Balance distributes weight so no part unfairly dominates.

questions.question: When all parts of an artwork feel like they belong together, the work has ____.
questions.memo: Unity = a coherent whole.

questions.question: Contrast can be created using opposite tones, colours or sizes.
questions.memo: Contrast comes from opposites — light/dark, big/small, bright/dull.

questions.question: Variation of paper size and format affects…
options: the scale and impact of the artwork
questions.expected: the scale and impact of the artwork
questions.memo: Different sizes and formats change how big and how detailed a work can be.

questions.question: Which best shows EMPHASIS?
options: One large red figure among small grey ones
All figures the same size and colour
questions.expected: One large red figure among small grey ones
questions.memo: A standout figure becomes the focal point — emphasis.

questions.question: Design principles can be used both to MAKE and to JUDGE an artwork.
questions.memo: You use principles to create work and to critique it.

questions.question: Which principle is mainly about guiding the viewer's EYE?
questions.memo: Movement leads the eye through the composition.

questions.question: Match each description to its design principle.

items.text: Repeated shapes lead the eye across
A bright focal point stands out
All parts feel like they belong together
A path your eye follows around the work

questions.expected: Repetition/eye-paths = rhythm & movement; a standout = emphasis; coherence = unity.
questions.memo: Rhythm/movement guide the eye; emphasis makes a focal point; unity ties it together.

questions.question: Why use design principles when planning an artwork?
options: They help the work communicate clearly and look intentional
questions.expected: They help the work communicate clearly and look intentional
questions.memo: Principles make a composition clear, organised and deliberate.

questions.question: Repeating shapes to lead the viewer's eye across a work creates…
questions.memo: Repetition that guides the eye creates visual rhythm and movement.

CA.G8.VAM.A1.title: Drawing, painting and media
CA.G8.VAM.A1.description: Visual Arts (CAPS G8) — Making in 2D & 3D: Drawing, painting and media.
CA.G8.VAM.A1.recovery_strategy: Trying different media, scales and formats widens what your drawing and painting can express.

questions.question: Using a 'wider range of media' means an artist…
options: works with more kinds of materials and techniques
questions.expected: works with more kinds of materials and techniques
questions.memo: Extending media means exploring more materials and techniques.

questions.question: 'Mixed media' artwork uses…
options: more than one material combined (e.g. paint and collage)
questions.expected: more than one material combined (e.g. paint and collage)
questions.memo: Mixed media combines materials, like paint with collage or ink.

questions.question: 'Collage' is made by…
options: sticking down pieces of paper or material
questions.expected: sticking down pieces of paper or material
questions.memo: Collage assembles cut or torn materials onto a surface.

questions.question: Changing the 'format' of a work means changing its…
options: shape and orientation (e.g. tall, wide, square)
questions.expected: shape and orientation (e.g. tall, wide, square)
questions.memo: Format is the shape/orientation — portrait, landscape, square.

questions.question: Working at a larger SCALE lets you include more detail and impact.
questions.memo: A larger scale gives room for more detail and a bigger impact.

questions.question: 'Lettering and design' combines…
options: words and images in one artwork
questions.expected: words and images in one artwork
questions.memo: Lettering projects blend text with images.

questions.question: Sticking down cut paper and materials makes a ____.
questions.memo: Assembling stuck-down pieces is collage.

questions.question: Etching techniques create an image by…
options: scratching or cutting lines into a surface
questions.expected: scratching or cutting lines into a surface
questions.memo: Etching scratches or cuts lines to make an image, as on scraperboard.

questions.question: Using extended techniques helps an artist express more complex ideas.
questions.memo: A wider technique range lets you express richer ideas.

questions.question: Brush manipulation includes changing the…
options: pressure, angle and stroke of the brush
questions.expected: pressure, angle and stroke of the brush
questions.memo: Controlling pressure, angle and stroke gives different brush effects.

questions.question: Which is an example of MIXED media?
options: A painting with collage and ink added
questions.expected: A painting with collage and ink added
questions.memo: Combining paint, collage and ink is mixed media.

questions.question: A portrait format is taller than it is wide.
questions.memo: Portrait orientation is vertical (taller than wide); landscape is horizontal.

questions.question: The shape and orientation of an artwork is its ____.
questions.memo: Format = shape/orientation.

questions.question: Experimenting with media is valuable because it…
options: helps you discover new effects and possibilities
questions.expected: helps you discover new effects and possibilities
questions.memo: Experimenting reveals new effects and expands what you can do.

questions.question: Pattern-making can be used to…
options: decorate a surface with repeated motifs
questions.expected: decorate a surface with repeated motifs
questions.memo: Pattern-making repeats motifs to decorate a surface.

questions.question: Combining drawing and painting techniques is allowed in one artwork.
questions.memo: Artists often combine drawing and painting in a single piece.

questions.question: A larger sheet of paper allows for…
questions.memo: Bigger paper gives room for larger marks and more detail.

questions.question: Sort each into a 2D MEDIUM/technique or a 3D one.
questions.expected: Collage and painting are 2D; clay modelling and construction are 3D.
questions.memo: Flat surface work is 2D; solid built or modelled work is 3D.

questions.question: Why explore a wider range of media in Grade 8?
options: To build skill and expand how you can express ideas
questions.expected: To build skill and expand how you can express ideas
questions.memo: A wider media range grows skill and expressive range.

questions.question: Sticking down cut or torn paper and materials makes a…
questions.memo: Assembling stuck-down pieces is a collage.

CA.G8.VAM.A2.title: Making in 3D
CA.G8.VAM.A2.description: Visual Arts (CAPS G8) — Making in 2D & 3D: Making in 3D.
CA.G8.VAM.A2.recovery_strategy: More complex 3D work deepens spatial awareness; good craftsmanship, safety and recycling still matter.

questions.question: More 'complex construction' in 3D means…
options: joining and building forms in more advanced ways
questions.expected: joining and building forms in more advanced ways
questions.memo: Complex construction builds richer 3D forms by joining materials skilfully.

questions.question: 'Modelling' a form means…
options: shaping a material like clay into a 3D form
questions.expected: shaping a material like clay into a 3D form
questions.memo: Modelling shapes a soft material into a 3D form.

questions.question: Deepening 'spatial awareness' means understanding…
options: depth, space and how forms relate in 3D
questions.expected: depth, space and how forms relate in 3D
questions.memo: Spatial awareness is sensing depth and the relationships of forms in space.

questions.question: Themes from the 'social world' for an artwork could include…
options: community life, friendship or popular culture
questions.expected: community life, friendship or popular culture
questions.memo: Social-world themes explore community, relationships and popular culture.

questions.question: Good craftsmanship and safety precautions still matter at Grade 8.
questions.memo: Care, skill and safety remain important as work becomes more complex.

questions.question: Using recyclable materials in 3D work shows…
questions.memo: Reusing recyclables shows environmental concern.

questions.question: Shaping clay into a 3D form is called ____.
questions.memo: Modelling shapes material into form.

questions.question: Manipulating a 'variety of materials and tools' means…
options: using and controlling different materials skilfully
questions.expected: using and controlling different materials skilfully
questions.memo: It means working confidently with many materials and tools.

questions.question: A 3D artwork can be viewed from more than one angle.
questions.memo: Three-dimensional works have many viewpoints, unlike a flat picture.

questions.question: Which is the SAFE way to use a sharp tool?
options: Cut away from your body and keep fingers clear
questions.expected: Cut away from your body and keep fingers clear
questions.memo: Always cut away from yourself and keep hands clear — basic tool safety.

questions.question: Construction and modelling both help develop…
questions.memo: Building and shaping forms deepens spatial awareness.

questions.question: Planning a 3D piece with sketches helps you build it more successfully.
questions.memo: Sketching the form first helps you build it well.

questions.question: A sculpture about friendship explores a theme from the…
questions.memo: Friendship is a social-world theme.

questions.question: Reusing boxes and bottle tops in art uses ____ materials.
questions.memo: Found, reusable materials are recyclable materials.

questions.question: 'Manipulating' materials means…
options: bending, joining or shaping them on purpose
questions.expected: bending, joining or shaping them on purpose
questions.memo: Manipulating is deliberately bending, joining and shaping materials.

questions.question: More complex 3D work usually needs more careful planning.
questions.memo: Complex forms need more planning to build successfully.

questions.question: Why keep the workspace tidy when making 3D art?
options: For safety and to care for tools and materials
questions.expected: For safety and to care for tools and materials
questions.memo: A tidy space is safer and protects tools and materials.

questions.question: Sort each action into GOOD craftsmanship/safety or POOR practice.
questions.expected: Cutting away and storing tools are good; leaving sharp tools out and rushing are poor.
questions.memo: Good craftsmanship means careful, safe, tidy work.

questions.question: Why explore themes from the social world in art?
options: Art can express ideas about the community and the world around us
questions.expected: Art can express ideas about the community and the world around us
questions.memo: Social themes let art comment on community and the wider world.

questions.question: Using recyclable materials in a sculpture shows concern for the environment.
questions.memo: Reusing recyclables reduces waste and shows environmental care.

CA.G8.VAL.A1.title: Looking and analysing
CA.G8.VAL.A1.description: Visual Arts (CAPS G8) — Visual literacy: Looking and analysing.
CA.G8.VAL.A1.recovery_strategy: Reading design means asking how something looks AND how it works; many careers, like fashion, blend both.

questions.question: 'Creative lettering' is…
options: designing letters in interesting, decorative ways
questions.expected: designing letters in interesting, decorative ways
questions.memo: Creative lettering treats letters as a designed, decorative image.

questions.question: A 'functional container' is an object that is…
options: both useful AND designed to look good
questions.expected: both useful AND designed to look good
questions.memo: A functional container does a job (holds things) and is well designed.

questions.question: 'Form follows function' suggests a designed object's shape should…
options: suit the job it has to do
questions.expected: suit the job it has to do
questions.memo: Good design shapes an object to serve its purpose well.

questions.question: 'Fashion design' is a career that involves…
questions.memo: Fashion designers create clothing and accessories.

questions.question: Analysing design means asking how something LOOKS and how it WORKS.
questions.memo: Design analysis considers both appearance and function.

questions.question: A jug that is both useful and well-designed is a functional ____.
questions.memo: A useful, designed object like a jug is a functional container.

questions.question: Decorative, designed letters on a poster are an example of…
questions.memo: Designed poster letters are creative lettering.

questions.question: When you analyse a designed object, you might consider its…
questions.memo: Design analysis looks at shape, materials, colour and purpose.

questions.question: Careers in the arts include fashion design, graphic design and illustration.
questions.memo: These are all real arts-and-design careers.

questions.question: Symbolic language in a logo means the logo…
options: uses images to stand for ideas about the brand
questions.expected: uses images to stand for ideas about the brand
questions.memo: Logos use symbols to communicate ideas about a brand.

questions.question: A good container design balances…
options: how it looks with how well it works
questions.expected: how it looks with how well it works
questions.memo: Good design balances appearance and function.

questions.question: You can express opinions about design by talking and writing about it.
questions.memo: Communicating views in talk and writing is part of visual literacy.

questions.question: Creative lettering might change a letter's…
questions.memo: Creative lettering plays with shape, colour, texture and decoration.

questions.question: Designing clothing is a career in ____ design.
questions.memo: Designing clothing is fashion design.

questions.question: Why does a designer think about MATERIALS for a container?
options: Materials affect how it works, lasts and looks
questions.expected: Materials affect how it works, lasts and looks
questions.memo: Material choice affects function, durability and appearance.

questions.question: A well-designed object can be both beautiful and useful.
questions.memo: Good design unites beauty and usefulness.

questions.question: Looking at a range of designs helps you…
options: learn what works and get ideas for your own
questions.expected: learn what works and get ideas for your own
questions.memo: Studying designs teaches what works and sparks ideas.

questions.question: Sort each item into a DESIGNED OBJECT or a CAREER in the arts.
questions.expected: Containers and posters are designed objects; fashion and graphic designers are careers.
questions.memo: Objects are things that are designed; careers are the jobs of the designers.

questions.question: Why is it useful to analyse both art AND design?
options: Design adds the question of how well something works, not just how it looks
questions.expected: Design adds the question of how well something works, not just how it looks
questions.memo: Analysing design adds function to the appearance you analyse in art.

questions.question: A jug that is both useful and well-designed is a…
questions.memo: A useful, well-designed object like a jug is a functional container.

CA.G8.VAL.A2.title: The artist, research and planning
CA.G8.VAL.A2.description: Visual Arts (CAPS G8) — Visual literacy: The artist, research and planning.
CA.G8.VAL.A2.recovery_strategy: Planning a project means collecting resources, references and rough sketches before the final work.

questions.question: In the WIDER society, an artist can act as a…
options: contributor and observer beyond their own community
questions.expected: contributor and observer beyond their own community
questions.memo: Artists contribute to and observe the wider society, not just their immediate community.

questions.question: 'Developing research skills' means getting better at…
options: finding and using reliable information and references
questions.expected: finding and using reliable information and references
questions.memo: Research skills grow by learning to find and use trustworthy sources.

questions.question: 'Planning and preparation' for a project includes…
options: collecting resources, references and preliminary sketches
questions.expected: collecting resources, references and preliminary sketches
questions.memo: Planning gathers resources, references and rough sketches before the final work.

questions.question: A 'preliminary sketch' is…
options: a rough drawing made to plan the final piece
questions.expected: a rough drawing made to plan the final piece
questions.memo: Preliminary sketches are rough planning drawings.

questions.question: Gathering reference images BEFORE making art improves the final result.
questions.memo: Good references and planning lead to a stronger final artwork.

questions.question: Rough drawings made to plan a final artwork are ____ sketches.
questions.memo: Preliminary = planning sketches.

questions.question: Reliable sources for art research include…
options: books, galleries, museums and trustworthy websites
questions.expected: books, galleries, museums and trustworthy websites
questions.memo: Books, galleries, museums and reliable sites are solid sources.

questions.question: 'Careers in the arts and design fields' include…
questions.memo: Arts and design careers are wide — architecture, animation, illustration and more.

questions.question: Keeping a sketchbook helps an artist plan and develop ideas.
questions.memo: A sketchbook records and develops ideas and references.

questions.question: With GUIDANCE in Grade 8, learners plan a project by…
options: collecting resources and making preliminary work for the final pieces
questions.expected: collecting resources and making preliminary work for the final pieces
questions.memo: Grade 8 learners plan with some guidance, preparing for the final work.

questions.question: Why research an artist before making work in their style?
options: To understand their techniques and ideas
questions.expected: To understand their techniques and ideas
questions.memo: Studying an artist reveals techniques and ideas you can learn from.

questions.question: Planning helps avoid mistakes and saves materials.
questions.memo: Good planning reduces mistakes and waste.

questions.question: An artist in the WIDER society might comment on…
options: issues that affect many people, not just their street
questions.expected: issues that affect many people, not just their street
questions.memo: Wider-society artists engage with broader issues.

questions.question: Finding and using reliable information for a project is doing ____.
questions.memo: Gathering reliable information is research.

questions.question: Which is part of GOOD preparation for an artwork?
options: Starting the final piece with no plan
questions.memo: Good preparation gathers references and explores ideas in sketches.

questions.question: Art and design careers can use both creativity and research.
questions.memo: Most arts careers blend creative making with research and planning.

questions.question: Why is planning especially important for a big project?
options: It organises the steps and resources before you commit
questions.expected: It organises the steps and resources before you commit
questions.memo: Planning organises a complex project before you start making.

questions.question: Put the planning steps for an art project in order.

items.text: Prepare materials and begin the final work

questions.expected: Theme, research, preliminary sketches, then prepare and make the final work.
questions.memo: Plan thoroughly before making: theme → research → sketches → final piece.

questions.question: Sort each into RESEARCH/PLANNING or FINAL MAKING.
questions.expected: References and sketches are planning; the final painting or sculpture is making.
questions.memo: Research and sketches come first; the final piece is the making.

questions.question: Rough drawings made to plan a final artwork are called…
questions.memo: Preliminary sketches are rough planning drawings made before the final work.

CA.G9.MUL.A1.title: Scales in treble and bass clef
CA.G9.MUL.A1.description: Music (CAPS G9) — Music literacy: Scales in treble and bass clef.
CA.G9.MUL.A1.recovery_strategy: The same scale can be written in either clef — the note names are the same, the staff position differs.

questions.question: Writing a scale in BOTH the treble and bass clefs means…
options: the same notes are written using each clef
the notes are different in each clef
only the treble clef is used
questions.expected: the same notes are written using each clef
questions.memo: The scale's notes stay the same; only the clef (and staff position) changes.

questions.question: Which scale has no sharps or flats in either clef?
questions.memo: C major has no sharps or flats, in any clef.

questions.question: In the bass clef, the note names are the same letters as the treble clef but…
options: sit in different positions on the staff
questions.expected: sit in different positions on the staff
questions.memo: Both clefs use A–G; the clef just changes where each note sits.

questions.question: G major has the sharp F# whether it is written in the treble or bass clef.
questions.memo: The key's sharps/flats stay the same in both clefs.

questions.question: Why write music in the bass clef?
questions.memo: The bass clef writes lower pitches without lots of ledger lines.

questions.question: The scale of ____ major has no sharps or flats in any clef.
questions.memo: C major is the all-natural scale.

questions.question: F major in either clef contains the flat…
questions.memo: F major flattens B in both clefs.

questions.question: D major in either clef contains the sharps…
questions.memo: D major has F# and C#, in both clefs.

questions.question: A scale written in the bass clef sounds higher than the same scale in the treble clef.
questions.memo: The bass clef writes LOWER pitches; same letters, but lower in sound.

questions.question: Both clefs together (treble on top, bass below) form a…
questions.memo: The treble and bass clefs joined make the grand staff, used for piano.

questions.question: A major scale always has how many notes before it repeats?
questions.memo: Seven different notes, then the octave repeats the first.

questions.question: The treble clef on top and bass clef below together make the ____ staff.
questions.memo: Together they form the grand staff.

questions.question: You can write the C major scale starting from middle C upward in the treble clef.
questions.memo: C major can be written ascending from middle C in the treble clef.

questions.question: Why learn to write scales in both clefs?
options: So you can read and write music for high and low instruments
questions.expected: So you can read and write music for high and low instruments
questions.memo: Both clefs let you handle the full range of high and low instruments.

questions.question: Which scales do you write in both clefs at Grade 9?
options: C, G, D and F major
questions.expected: C, G, D and F major
questions.memo: Grade 9 covers C, G, D and F major in both clefs.

questions.question: The sharps or flats of a scale are the same no matter which clef it is written in.
questions.memo: A key's sharps/flats are fixed regardless of clef.

questions.question: Middle C sits…
options: between the treble and bass clefs on the grand staff
at the top of the treble clef
questions.expected: between the treble and bass clefs on the grand staff
questions.memo: Middle C sits on a ledger line between the two clefs.

questions.question: Sort each scale by its sharps or flats (in any clef).
questions.expected: C none; G and D have sharps; F has a flat — the same in both clefs.
questions.memo: Sharps/flats belong to the key, not the clef.

questions.question: The grand staff is mainly used for which instrument?
questions.memo: The piano uses the grand staff — treble for the right hand, bass for the left.

questions.question: The treble and bass clefs written together form the…
questions.memo: The two clefs joined make the grand staff, used for piano.

CA.G9.MUL.A2.title: Key signatures
CA.G9.MUL.A2.description: Music (CAPS G9) — Music literacy: Key signatures.
CA.G9.MUL.A2.recovery_strategy: A key signature lists the sharps or flats for a key: C has none, G has F#, D has F# and C#, F has B flat.

questions.question: A 'key signature' is…
options: the sharps or flats written at the start of each line
questions.expected: the sharps or flats written at the start of each line
questions.memo: The key signature shows the key's sharps/flats once, at the start of every line.

questions.question: The key signature of C major has…
questions.memo: C major's key signature is empty — no sharps or flats.

questions.question: The key signature of G major has…
questions.memo: G major has one sharp: F#.

questions.question: The key signature of D major has…
questions.memo: D major has two sharps: F# and C#.

questions.question: The key signature of F major has…
questions.memo: F major has one flat: B flat.

questions.question: A key signature saves you writing the same sharp or flat in front of every note.
questions.memo: Writing the sharps/flats once at the start applies them throughout.

questions.question: G major's key signature contains the sharp ____.
questions.memo: G major's single sharp is F#.

questions.question: F major's key signature contains the flat ____.
questions.memo: F major's single flat is B flat.

questions.question: If you see two sharps, F# and C#, the key is…
questions.memo: Two sharps (F#, C#) indicate D major.

questions.question: The key signature appears…
options: at the start of every line, after the clef
only once in the whole piece
questions.expected: at the start of every line, after the clef
questions.memo: The key signature is written after the clef at the start of each line.

questions.question: C major and A minor share the same (empty) key signature.
questions.memo: A minor is the relative minor of C major and shares its empty key signature.

questions.question: Which key signature has the MOST sharps among C, G and D major?
questions.memo: D major has two sharps, more than G (one) or C (none).

questions.question: A key signature with one flat (B flat) tells you the key is likely…
questions.memo: One flat, B flat, points to F major.

questions.question: The key signature affects every note of that letter name throughout the piece.
questions.memo: A sharp/flat in the key signature applies to that note in every octave, all through.

questions.question: Why are key signatures useful?
options: They make music quicker to read and write
questions.expected: They make music quicker to read and write
questions.memo: Stating the sharps/flats once speeds up reading and writing.

questions.question: The key of ____ major has an empty key signature.
questions.memo: C major has no sharps or flats.

questions.question: If a melody has no sharps or flats marked at the start, it could be in…
questions.memo: An empty key signature suggests C major (or A minor).

questions.question: Match each key to its key signature.
questions.expected: C major = none; G major = F#; F major = B flat.
questions.memo: C none, G one sharp (F#), F one flat (B flat).

questions.question: Order these keys from FEWEST to MOST sharps.
questions.expected: C major (0), G major (1), D major (2).
questions.memo: Each step round the sharp keys adds one sharp: C, G, D.

questions.question: A key signature with one sharp (F#) usually means the key is…
questions.memo: One sharp, F#, points to G major.

CA.G9.MUL.A3.title: Ledger lines
CA.G9.MUL.A3.description: Music (CAPS G9) — Music literacy: Ledger lines.
CA.G9.MUL.A3.recovery_strategy: Ledger lines extend the staff so you can write notes that are too high or too low to fit on it.

questions.question: 'Ledger lines' are…
options: short extra lines for notes above or below the staff
questions.expected: short extra lines for notes above or below the staff
questions.memo: Ledger lines extend the staff so very high or low notes can be written.

questions.question: Ledger lines are used when a note is…
options: too high or too low to fit on the staff
questions.expected: too high or too low to fit on the staff
questions.memo: They are added when notes go beyond the five staff lines.

questions.question: Middle C in the treble clef sits on…
options: one ledger line below the staff
questions.expected: one ledger line below the staff
questions.memo: Middle C is one ledger line below the treble staff.

questions.question: Ledger lines can be added both above AND below the staff.
questions.memo: Notes above and below the staff both use ledger lines.

questions.question: Each ledger line continues the pattern of…
options: lines and spaces beyond the staff
questions.expected: lines and spaces beyond the staff
questions.memo: Ledger lines keep the line-space pattern going past the staff edge.

questions.question: Short extra lines for very high or low notes are ____ lines.
questions.memo: These extra lines are ledger lines.

questions.question: A note sitting two ledger lines above the treble staff is…
options: higher than one sitting on the top line
questions.expected: higher than one sitting on the top line
questions.memo: The further above the staff, the higher the pitch.

questions.question: Ledger lines make it possible to write notes outside the normal five-line staff.
questions.memo: They extend the range beyond the five lines.

questions.question: Why not just add more permanent lines to the staff?
options: Too many lines would be hard to read; ledger lines are added only when needed
questions.expected: Too many lines would be hard to read; ledger lines are added only when needed
questions.memo: A staff stays at five lines for clarity; ledger lines appear only as needed.

questions.question: Below the bass clef, ledger lines show notes that are…
questions.memo: Ledger lines below the bass staff show the lowest pitches.

questions.question: The more ledger lines above the staff, the higher the note.
questions.memo: Extra ledger lines above mean higher pitches.

questions.question: Middle C sits one ledger line ____ the treble staff.
questions.memo: Middle C is one ledger line below the treble staff.

questions.question: Ledger lines are drawn…
options: only as long as the note needs
questions.expected: only as long as the note needs
questions.memo: Each ledger line is short — just wide enough for its note.

questions.question: Ledger lines help connect the treble and bass clefs around middle C.
questions.memo: Middle C and nearby notes use ledger lines bridging the two clefs.

questions.question: A singer with a very high part might see notes written on…
options: ledger lines below the bass clef
questions.memo: Very high notes appear on ledger lines above the staff.

questions.question: Reading ledger-line notes gets easier if you…
options: count up or down line-by-line from a note you know
questions.expected: count up or down line-by-line from a note you know
questions.memo: Counting steps from a known note helps you read ledger-line pitches.

questions.question: Ledger lines change how LOUD a note is.
questions.memo: Ledger lines change PITCH (high/low), not loudness.

questions.question: Sort each statement about ledger lines as TRUE or FALSE.

items.text: They extend the staff for high/low notes
They can go above and below
They run across the whole page

questions.expected: Ledger lines extend the staff above and below (true); they don't change volume or span the page (false).
questions.memo: Ledger lines extend pitch range; short lines, above or below, no effect on volume.

questions.question: Why are ledger lines important for instruments with a wide range?
options: They let very high and very low notes be written clearly
questions.expected: They let very high and very low notes be written clearly
questions.memo: Wide-range instruments need ledger lines to notate their extreme pitches.

questions.question: Ledger lines let you write notes that are too high or too low for the staff.
questions.memo: Ledger lines extend the staff for notes beyond its five lines.

CA.G9.MUL.A4.title: Intervals
CA.G9.MUL.A4.recovery_strategy: An interval is counted by including both notes: C up to G is a 5th (C-D-E-F-G).

questions.question: An 'interval' is…
questions.memo: An interval is the pitch distance between two notes.

questions.question: To count an interval, you count…
options: both the bottom and top notes (and all in between)
questions.expected: both the bottom and top notes (and all in between)
questions.memo: Include both notes: C up to E is a 3rd (C-D-E).

questions.question: The interval from C up to G is a…
questions.memo: C-D-E-F-G = five notes, a 5th.

questions.question: The interval from C up to E is a…
questions.memo: C-D-E = three notes, a 3rd.

questions.question: Two notes of the same pitch form a…
questions.memo: The same note twice is a unison (a 1st).

questions.question: From one C up to the next C is an…
questions.memo: C to the C above spans eight notes — an octave.

questions.question: The distance between two notes is called an ____.
questions.memo: The pitch distance is an interval.

questions.question: The interval C up to F is a…
questions.memo: C-D-E-F = four notes, a 4th.

questions.question: The interval D up to A is a…
questions.memo: D-E-F-G-A = five notes, a 5th.

questions.question: C up to D is a 2nd.
questions.memo: C-D = two notes, a 2nd.

questions.question: To name an interval you only count the top note.
questions.memo: You count BOTH notes and everything between them.

questions.question: A 'melodic' interval is one where the two notes are…
questions.memo: Melodic intervals sound one note then the next; harmonic intervals sound together.

questions.question: A 'harmonic' interval is one where the two notes are…
questions.memo: Harmonic intervals sound the two notes together.

questions.question: From one note up to the same note an octave higher is an ____.
questions.memo: The eight-note span is an octave.

questions.question: The interval E up to G is a…
questions.memo: E-F-G = three notes, a 3rd.

questions.question: A 5th is a bigger interval than a 3rd.
questions.memo: A 5th spans five notes; a 3rd spans three — the 5th is bigger.

questions.question: Why are intervals useful to know?
options: They help you build chords and read melodies
questions.expected: They help you build chords and read melodies
questions.memo: Intervals are the building blocks of chords and melodies.

questions.question: Match each note pair to its interval (counting up).
questions.memo: Count both notes: 2 letters = 2nd, 3 letters = 3rd, 5 letters = 5th.

questions.question: Counting C-D-E-F-G, the interval C to G is a 5th because…
options: there are five note names from C to G
questions.expected: there are five note names from C to G
questions.memo: Five note names (C,D,E,F,G) means a 5th.

questions.question: Counting C-D-E, the interval from C up to E is a…
questions.memo: Three note names (C, D, E) make a 3rd.

CA.G9.MUL.A5.title: Triads
CA.G9.MUL.A5.recovery_strategy: A triad stacks three notes a third apart: the root, the note two letters up, and the note four letters up.

questions.question: A 'triad' is…
questions.memo: A triad is a chord of three notes.

questions.question: A triad is built from the…
questions.memo: A triad stacks the root, the note a 3rd above, and the note a 5th above.

questions.question: The bottom (lowest) note of a triad is the…
questions.memo: The root is the lowest note that names the chord.

questions.question: The notes of a C major triad are…
questions.memo: C major triad = C (root), E (3rd), G (5th).

questions.question: In a triad, each note is a __ apart.
questions.memo: Triad notes are stacked in thirds: root, +3rd, +3rd again.

questions.question: A chord of three notes is a ____.
questions.memo: Three-note chord = triad.

questions.question: The notes of a G major triad are…
questions.memo: G major triad = G (root), B (3rd), D (5th).

questions.question: The notes of an F major triad are…
questions.memo: F major triad = F (root), A (3rd), C (5th).

questions.question: A triad has three notes stacked in thirds.
questions.memo: Triad = three notes a 3rd apart (root, 3rd, 5th).

questions.question: The middle note of a triad is the…
questions.memo: The middle note is the 3rd above the root.

questions.question: The top note of a major triad is the…
questions.memo: The top note is the 5th above the root.

questions.question: C, E and G played together form the C major triad.
questions.memo: C-E-G is the C major triad.

questions.question: The lowest note that names a triad is the ____.
questions.memo: The root names and grounds the triad.

questions.question: The D major triad contains…
questions.memo: D major triad = D, F# (3rd), A (5th) — F is sharp in D major.

questions.question: A triad and an interval are the same thing.
questions.memo: An interval is TWO notes; a triad is THREE notes.

questions.question: Triads are important because they…
options: form the chords that harmonise melodies
questions.expected: form the chords that harmonise melodies
questions.memo: Triads are the basic chords used to harmonise music.

questions.question: To build a triad on any note, add the notes…
options: a 3rd and a 5th above the root
questions.expected: a 3rd and a 5th above the root
questions.memo: Stack a 3rd and 5th above the root to build the triad.

questions.question: Match each triad to its notes.

items.text: Root C, third E, fifth G

questions.expected: C major = C-E-G; G major = G-B-D; F major = F-A-C.
questions.memo: Each triad is root + 3rd + 5th.

questions.question: Build the C major triad: order the notes from LOWEST to highest.
questions.memo: A triad stacks root, third, fifth from the bottom up.

questions.question: The three notes of a C major triad are…
questions.memo: A C major triad is the root C, the 3rd E and the 5th G.

CA.G9.MUL.A6.title: Writing scales rhythmically
CA.G9.MUL.A6.description: Music (CAPS G9) — Music literacy: Writing scales rhythmically.
CA.G9.MUL.A6.recovery_strategy: Writing a scale rhythmically combines the right pitches with chosen note values in a bar.

questions.question: 'Writing a scale rhythmically' means writing its notes…
options: using chosen note values, not just plain noteheads
questions.expected: using chosen note values, not just plain noteheads
questions.memo: You write the scale's pitches using note values (crotchets, quavers, etc.).

questions.question: If you write a C major scale in crotchets in 4/4, how many bars do the 8 notes fill?
questions.memo: Eight crotchets at four per bar fill two bars.

questions.question: To write a scale rhythmically you combine…
options: the right pitches with note values
questions.expected: the right pitches with note values
questions.memo: It joins correct pitches with chosen rhythms.

questions.question: A scale can be written using note values learnt in earlier grades, like crotchets and quavers.
questions.memo: You apply known note values to the scale's pitches.

questions.question: Which scales do you write rhythmically at Grade 9?
options: C, G, D and F major
questions.expected: C, G, D and F major
questions.memo: Grade 9 writes C, G, D and F major scales rhythmically.

questions.question: Writing a scale with crotchets and quavers gives it a ____.
questions.memo: Adding note values gives the scale a rhythm.

questions.question: If you write a scale in quavers, the notes will sound…
questions.memo: Quavers are short, so the scale moves faster.

questions.question: Each bar of a rhythmic scale must add up to the beats in the time signature.
questions.memo: Every bar's note values must total the bar's beats.

questions.question: A C major scale up and down (15 notes) written in crotchets needs the right number of…
options: bars to hold all the beats
questions.expected: bars to hold all the beats
questions.memo: You need enough bars to contain all the crotchet beats.

questions.question: Writing scales rhythmically combines two skills:
questions.memo: It brings together pitch and rhythm.

questions.question: You can write the F major scale rhythmically, remembering the B flat.
questions.memo: F major's B flat applies even when the scale is written with rhythm.

questions.question: To write a scale rhythmically you need the correct pitches AND the correct note ____.
questions.memo: Pitches plus note values make a rhythmic scale.

questions.question: Which note value would make a scale sound slowest?
questions.memo: Minims (2 beats each) are the longest here, so the scale moves slowest.

questions.question: A rhythmic scale still goes up (or down) step by step in pitch.
questions.memo: The pitches still move by step; only the rhythm is added.

questions.question: Why practise writing scales rhythmically?
options: It links your knowledge of pitch and rhythm together
questions.expected: It links your knowledge of pitch and rhythm together
questions.memo: It combines pitch and rhythm skills in one task.

questions.question: If a bar of 4/4 holds a scale fragment of four notes, each note is a…
questions.memo: Four equal notes in a 4/4 bar are crotchets (one beat each).

questions.question: Note values can be mixed (e.g. some crotchets, some quavers) when writing a scale rhythmically.
questions.memo: You may mix values as long as each bar adds up correctly.

questions.question: Sort each into PITCH information or RHYTHM information.

items.text: The notes C D E F G

questions.expected: Note names and sharps/flats are pitch; note values and beats are rhythm.
questions.memo: Pitch = which notes; rhythm = how long they last.

questions.question: A rhythmic scale that fits its time signature shows you understand…
questions.memo: Fitting the bars correctly proves you grasp scales and rhythm together.

questions.question: Writing a scale rhythmically means giving its notes chosen note values.
questions.memo: A rhythmic scale combines the scale's pitches with note values.

CA.G9.MUE.A1.title: Orchestral families
CA.G9.MUE.A1.description: Music (CAPS G9) — Listening & elements: Orchestral families.
CA.G9.MUE.A1.recovery_strategy: The orchestra groups instruments into strings, woodwind, brass and percussion by how they make their sound.

questions.question: The four families of the orchestra are…
questions.memo: The orchestra is grouped into strings, woodwind, brass and percussion.

questions.question: The STRINGS family makes sound by…
questions.memo: Strings (violin, cello) are bowed or plucked.

questions.question: The BRASS family makes sound by…
options: buzzing the lips into a metal mouthpiece
questions.expected: buzzing the lips into a metal mouthpiece
questions.memo: Brass players buzz their lips into a mouthpiece (trumpet, trombone, tuba).

questions.question: Which instrument belongs to the WOODWIND family?
questions.memo: The flute is a woodwind instrument (sounded by blown air).

questions.question: Which instrument belongs to the PERCUSSION family?
questions.memo: Timpani are struck — percussion.

questions.question: The violin, viola, cello and double bass all belong to the…
questions.memo: These bowed instruments are the string family.

questions.question: A trumpet and a trombone belong to the ____ family.
questions.memo: Trumpet and trombone are brass.

questions.question: The clarinet and oboe belong to the…
questions.memo: Clarinet and oboe are woodwind.

questions.question: Drums, cymbals and the xylophone are all percussion.
questions.memo: Struck instruments like these are percussion.

questions.question: Brass instruments are usually made of…
questions.memo: Brass instruments are metal, played by buzzing the lips.

questions.question: A flute is made of metal but is still a WOODWIND instrument.
questions.memo: The flute is classed as woodwind by how it is played, even though it's metal today.

questions.question: Which family usually keeps the rhythm and adds dramatic accents?
questions.memo: Percussion drives rhythm and provides accents in the orchestra.

questions.question: How is sound produced in the STRING family?
options: A vibrating string, bowed or plucked
questions.expected: A vibrating string, bowed or plucked
questions.memo: Strings sound from a vibrating string.

questions.question: The flute, clarinet and oboe belong to the ____ family.
questions.memo: These blown instruments are woodwind.

questions.question: Identifying instrument families by ear helps you follow what is happening in a piece.
questions.memo: Recognising families deepens your listening and understanding.

questions.question: The largest, lowest string instrument is the…
questions.memo: The double bass is the biggest and lowest of the strings.

questions.question: Why group orchestral instruments into families?
options: Instruments that make sound in similar ways behave and blend alike
questions.expected: Instruments that make sound in similar ways behave and blend alike
questions.memo: Families group instruments by how they produce sound, which shapes how they blend.

questions.question: Sort each instrument into its orchestral family.
questions.expected: Cello = strings, clarinet = woodwind, trumpet = brass, timpani = percussion.
questions.memo: Strings bowed, woodwind/brass blown, percussion struck.

questions.question: Brass and woodwind are both blown, but they make sound in different ways.
questions.memo: Brass buzzes the lips; woodwind uses an air stream or reed — both are blown, differently.

questions.question: The cello belongs to which orchestral family?
questions.memo: The cello is a bowed string instrument.

CA.G9.MUE.A2.title: Music styles
CA.G9.MUE.A2.description: Music (CAPS G9) — Listening & elements: Music styles.
CA.G9.MUE.A2.recovery_strategy: Each style has signature features; kwaito is slow South African house, reggae has its off-beat rhythm.

questions.question: 'Kwaito' is a music style that began in…
questions.memo: Kwaito is a South African style that grew in the 1990s.

questions.question: 'Reggae' originated in…
questions.memo: Reggae is a Jamaican style, known for its off-beat rhythm.

questions.question: Reggae is well known for its…
questions.memo: Reggae emphasises the off-beats, giving its relaxed, skanking groove.

questions.question: 'R&B' stands for…
questions.memo: R&B means Rhythm and Blues.

questions.question: 'African jazz' blends jazz with…
questions.memo: African jazz mixes jazz with African rhythmic and melodic features.

questions.question: Kwaito usually has a slow, laid-back tempo with repeated grooves.
questions.memo: Kwaito is known for slowed-down, looping house grooves.

questions.question: A South African style that grew in the 1990s is ____.
questions.memo: Kwaito is the South African 1990s style.

questions.question: When describing a style, you might note its…
questions.memo: You describe a style by its rhythm, tempo, instruments and vocal features.

questions.question: Different styles can be recognised by their typical instruments and rhythms.
questions.memo: Each style has signature instruments and rhythmic feels.

questions.question: The 'special features' of a style include things like…
options: its rhythm and the instruments used
questions.expected: its rhythm and the instruments used
questions.memo: Special features are the rhythmic and instrumental hallmarks of a style.

questions.question: Writing your 'own impression' of a song means describing…
options: how it sounds and makes you feel
questions.expected: how it sounds and makes you feel
questions.memo: Your impression captures the sound and the feelings the music gives you.

questions.question: Reggae and kwaito have different rhythmic feels.
questions.memo: Reggae's off-beat differs from kwaito's slow looping groove.

questions.question: R&B often features…
options: smooth vocals and a strong groove
questions.expected: smooth vocals and a strong groove
questions.memo: R&B is known for smooth, expressive vocals over a strong groove.

questions.question: The off-beat rhythm is a signature of ____ music.
questions.memo: Reggae's signature is its off-beat.

questions.question: Listening to a variety of styles helps you…
options: appreciate and describe different kinds of music
questions.expected: appreciate and describe different kinds of music
questions.memo: Wide listening builds appreciation and a vocabulary to describe music.

questions.question: Which feature would you listen for to identify a style's GROOVE?
questions.memo: A style's groove lives in its rhythm and beat.

questions.question: African jazz can include instruments from both jazz and African traditions.
questions.memo: It blends jazz instruments with African traditional sounds.

questions.question: Match each style to its origin or feature.

items.text: Slow looping groove from South Africa

questions.expected: Reggae = Jamaican off-beat; kwaito = SA slow groove; R&B = smooth Rhythm and Blues.
questions.memo: Each style has a home and a signature feel.

questions.question: Why describe the rhythm, tempo and instruments of a style?
options: These features help you recognise and compare styles
questions.expected: These features help you recognise and compare styles
questions.memo: These features are how you identify and compare musical styles.

questions.question: Kwaito is a music style that began in…
questions.memo: Kwaito grew in South Africa in the 1990s.

CA.G9.MUE.A3.title: Musicals, opera and the anthem
CA.G9.MUE.A3.description: Music (CAPS G9) — Listening & elements: Musicals, opera and the anthem.
CA.G9.MUE.A3.recovery_strategy: A musical or opera tells a story through song; the South African anthem joins five languages and two melodies.

questions.question: A 'musical' is a stage show that tells a story through…
questions.memo: A musical combines songs, dialogue and often dance to tell a story.

questions.question: An 'opera' is a stage work where the story is told mostly through…
questions.memo: In opera the drama is carried mostly by singing, with an orchestra.

questions.question: 'West Side Story' is an example of a…
questions.memo: West Side Story is a famous musical.

questions.question: 'The Magic Flute' is an example of an…
questions.memo: The Magic Flute (Mozart) is a famous opera.

questions.question: The 'storyline' of a musical or opera is…
options: the plot — what happens in the story
questions.expected: the plot — what happens in the story
questions.memo: The storyline is the plot that the music and drama tell.

questions.question: A 'chorus' in a musical/opera is…
questions.memo: The chorus is a large group of singers.

questions.question: A 'solo' is sung by…
questions.memo: A solo is sung by a single performer.

questions.question: The South African National Anthem combines five languages and two earlier melodies.
questions.memo: The anthem joins five languages and two songs (Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika and Die Stem).

questions.question: A stage story told mostly through singing is an ____.
questions.memo: Opera tells its story through singing.

questions.question: Both musicals and operas can tell a complete story with music.
questions.memo: Both forms tell full stories through music and drama.

questions.question: The main difference between a musical and an opera is that a musical…
questions.memo: Musicals mix spoken dialogue with songs; operas are mostly sung throughout.

questions.question: Singing along with a chorus from a musical helps you…
questions.memo: Joining in helps you feel and understand the music.

questions.question: An orchestra usually accompanies an opera.
questions.memo: Operas are typically accompanied by a full orchestra.

questions.question: Discussing the National Anthem, you might reflect on its…
questions.memo: Reflection on the anthem covers its meaning, languages and history.

questions.question: A large group of singers in a musical is the ____.
questions.memo: The chorus is the large group of singers.

questions.question: Following the storyline helps you understand why the songs happen.
questions.memo: Knowing the plot explains the songs' meaning and place.

questions.question: Why do people value works like West Side Story or The Magic Flute?
options: They combine music and drama to tell powerful stories
questions.expected: They combine music and drama to tell powerful stories
questions.memo: These works unite music and drama into powerful storytelling.

questions.question: Sort each work or term under MUSICAL or OPERA.
questions.expected: West Side Story and spoken dialogue = musical; The Magic Flute and mostly-sung = opera.
questions.memo: Musicals mix song and speech; operas are mostly sung.

questions.question: A 'storyline of a musical' would describe…
options: the characters and events in order
questions.expected: the characters and events in order
questions.memo: A storyline lays out the characters and events of the plot.

questions.question: A stage work whose story is told mostly through singing is an…
questions.memo: Opera carries its story mainly through singing.

CA.G9.MUP.A1.title: Composing
CA.G9.MUP.A1.recovery_strategy: Completing a phrase means writing an 'answer' that balances the opening; a jingle is a short, catchy advert tune.

questions.question: Completing a 'four-bar phrase' means writing music that…
options: answers and balances the opening bars
questions.expected: answers and balances the opening bars
questions.memo: You compose an 'answer' that balances the given opening to complete the phrase.

questions.question: In question-and-answer phrases, the answer usually…
options: ends in a settled, complete way
questions.expected: ends in a settled, complete way
questions.memo: The answering phrase resolves to feel complete.

questions.question: 'Adding music to words' means…
options: composing a melody to fit a set of lyrics
questions.expected: composing a melody to fit a set of lyrics
questions.memo: You write a tune that fits and expresses the words.

questions.question: A 'jingle' is…
options: a short, catchy tune for an advertisement
questions.expected: a short, catchy tune for an advertisement
questions.memo: A jingle is a short, memorable tune used to advertise a product or event.

questions.question: A good jingle is short and easy to remember.
questions.memo: Jingles work by being short and catchy so people remember them.

questions.question: A short catchy tune made to advertise something is a ____.
questions.memo: An advertising tune is a jingle.

questions.question: When you complete a four-bar phrase, your answer should match the opening's…
questions.memo: The answer should fit the opening's style and rhythm to balance it.

questions.question: Composing can be done in a group or on your own.
questions.memo: You can compose solo or collaboratively in a group.

questions.question: Setting a poem to music means…
options: writing a melody that fits the poem's words and mood
questions.expected: writing a melody that fits the poem's words and mood
questions.memo: You compose a melody that suits the poem's words and feeling.

questions.question: A good melody for words usually fits the…
options: natural rhythm and stress of the words
questions.expected: natural rhythm and stress of the words
questions.memo: Melodies for words follow the words' natural rhythm and stresses.

questions.question: An advertisement jingle often names or describes the product.
questions.memo: Jingles usually mention or describe the product or event.

questions.question: Repetition in a jingle helps because it…
questions.memo: Repeating the hook makes a jingle stick in memory.

questions.question: Composing an 'answer' to balance an opening completes a four-bar ____.
questions.memo: The opening plus answer complete the phrase.

questions.question: Which is the BEST first step when composing a melody for words?
options: Read the words and feel their rhythm and mood
questions.expected: Read the words and feel their rhythm and mood
questions.memo: Start by absorbing the words' rhythm and mood before writing the tune.

questions.question: You can compose using either standard notation or non-conventional notation.
questions.memo: Compositions may use standard notes or graphic/non-conventional notation.

questions.question: A jingle for a school fair would aim to…
options: make people remember and want to attend
questions.expected: make people remember and want to attend
questions.memo: An effective jingle is memorable and makes people want to act.

questions.question: Performing your composition lets others hear your musical ideas.
questions.memo: Performing shares your created music with an audience.

questions.question: Put the steps for composing a short advertisement jingle in order.

items.text: Decide on the product or event
Compose a simple, memorable tune for the words
Repeat the hook and perform it

questions.expected: Choose the product, write a catchy hook, set a memorable tune, then repeat and perform.
questions.memo: Jingles: product → hook → tune → repeat and perform.

questions.question: Sort each into part of COMPOSING for words/jingles or NOT.
